summary.text: Son of Laomedon (`laomedon`) who sat with Priam among the elders at the Scaean gates and father of Dolops (`dolops-trojan`), his bravest son, well skilled with the spear — distinct from Lampus, one of Hector's horses in *Iliad* 8.

story.text: About Priam and Panthous and Thymoetes and Lampus and Clytius and Hicetaon, scion of Ares, and Ucalegon and Antenor — men of prudence both — sat as elders of the people at the Scaean gates; because of old age had they now ceased from battle, but speakers they were full sweet.

When Meges son of Phyleus leapt upon Polydamas, Dolops son of Lampus — whom Lampus son of Laomedon begat, even his bravest son, well skilled in furious might — thrust with his spear full upon the shield of Phyleus' son from nigh at hand.
